prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Complete the “Tables 5 and 6 – Testing Results” for the sample screen. (This will all be automatic if you are using the Smart Inspection Transaction).

### Important notes:

- The Inspection # and the Sample dates and times must be accurate. All subsequent water-quality data from this inspection must be reported to the Ohio EPA within **48 hours** (2 business days) of the date and time of the failed test(s).

- Inspections must not contain more than one sample date. If there are multiple samples, then the inspection records must be split into separate inspections by sample date. Only the sample tests should be used to do this inspection split; laboratory tests belong with their respective sample inspections and should not be included as part of the inspection split. # Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

3. Complete the “Tables 5a and 6a – Microbiology Results” tab for all

refusal.explanation: There is no refusal; the text gives compliance-oriented instructions for documenting the failures.
